sections.name: Abhainn Deabhag
sections.notes: Gauging station long way below WW section and below confluence with Affric. Affric is usually dry due to dam so gauge is more useful for the abhainn deabhag but interpret with a pinch of salt. River drops fast.

sections.name: Aire — The "Wave"
sections.desc: Playspot near Leeds. Beautiful glassy wave if you catch it at the right level.
sections.directions: Playspot to the SE of Leeds, just downstream of Woodlesford rail station. From Aberford Rd (A642) head down Fleet Lane to the oil storage depot (just after the bridge over the canal). This is on an island formed by the canal and the river. Park up and walk downstream 200m to a bridge over the river to see if the wave is in condition.

sections.name: Allen — Cupola Bridge to South Tyne Confluence
sections.desc: A fun trib of the South Tyne, containing boulder garden rapids and a 6ft sloping weir (Hagg Fall).
sections.directions: Put in at Cupola Bridge. Take out either at Plankey Mill or continue down the South Tyne to Haydon Bridge.

sections.name: Almond (Lothian)
sections.notes: Large sewage spill mid-April 2020. Do not paddle.

sections.name: Almond (Perthshire)
sections.notes: No calibrations yet, please send them in

sections.name: Annan
sections.notes: 0.6 reported as Low. 1.46 as high. Please send more calibrations.

sections.name: Arkle Beck — Whaw to Swale Confluence
sections.desc: A trib of the Swale, which runs in high water. Starts off as fast continuous grade 3 from Whaw in decent water, with few eddies. Mellows a bit in the middle, and gets shallow where the river splits into various channels. Steeps up a bit again as you approach Reeth. There's one sheep fence to be aware of and trees are always going to be an issue, particuarly towards the end.
sections.directions: If the water is high put in at the road bridge in Whaw where there's space for a couple of cars, otherwise use the road bridge above Langthwaite. In very high water it may be possible to put-in even higher up for added fast grade 3. Take out either in Reeth or in Grinton after the Swale confluence, or continue down the Swale.

sections.name: Ashgill Beck — Ashgill Force to South Tyne Confluence
sections.desc: Short steep trib of the Upper South Tyne containing five falls. Usually paddled as a diversion to the Tyne.
sections.directions: Put on below Ashgill Force (it lands on rock). Continue down the South Tyne after the confluence.

sections.name: Averon of Alness
sections.notes: Updated calibrations 2021-10-31 Tree Reported 11 Feb 2020Wires reported March 9 2020

sections.name: Avon (Glasgow)
sections.notes: New calibrations Nov 2018, thanks Robin. Tree removed with funding from AJ Access Fund 2019

sections.name: Avon (Spey)
sections.notes: New entry Nov 2018. Please fill in calibration report to confirm/adjust.

sections.name: Ayr
sections.notes: New calibrations Jan 2019. Poorly calibrated, more calibrations welcome on this gauge and Catrine gauge. Ignore gauge calibration in guidebook which is wrong.

sections.name: Barle — Dulverton to Exebridge
sections.desc: The poor sibling to the section upstream, but runs at lower levels. A decent touring run or introduction for beginners. Watch out for a couple of weirs and takeout at Exebridge after the confluence with the Exe.
sections.directions: Putin at Dulverton, at the concrete ramp on river left just upstream of the main road bridge. Please park in the public carpark rather than the limited space by the river. Takeout in Exebridge river left just upstream of the bridge: the pub don't mind you using their carpark but consider a post-trip beer.

sections.name: Barle — Tarr Steps to Dulverton
sections.desc: The classic gd2 run of the south-west, and an excellent introduction to whitewater for beginners. The first km down from Tarr Steps holds the best rapids.
sections.directions: Putin at Tarr Steps, on the minor road between Hawkridge and Liscombe (south-east of Withypool). Takeout in Dulverton on river left just before the main bridge, using the public carpark rather than the limited parking by the river.

sections.name: Bedburn Beck — Source to Wear Confluence
sections.desc: Spate beck formed from the confluence of Euden and Spurlswood Becks in Hamsterley forest. A few gorgy sections of grade 3. Obviously trees can be an issue!
sections.directions: Put-in points at various places within Hamsterley forest. The highest available being the confluence of Euden and Spurlswood at Grove Park. Follow the Forest Drive through Hamsterley, use one of the car parks and put-on as high up as you feel like. Multiple get-outs from the bridge in Bedburn down to the Wear itself where it passes under the A68.

sections.name: Big Water of Fleet
sections.notes: New gauge 12/12/18, please send calibrations to confirm/adjust

sections.name: Blackwater (Garve)
sections.notes: Section moved to Blackwater (Garve) Middle Dec 2023. Please send calibrations to confirm.

sections.name: Blackwater (Garve) (Upper)
sections.notes: Only low-high is calibrated, more calibrations needed

sections.name: Blackwater (Perthshire)
sections.notes: Gauge is below confluence with River Ardle so may not be very accurate. Access link added Jan 2023. See also Paddle Scotland access request.

sections.name: Braan (Gorge)
sections.notes: See access issue link for reported tree constribtions Nov 2019 & Jan 2020

sections.name: Braan (Upper)
sections.notes: Gauge is far below so readings not always up to date

sections.name: Brathay — Elterwater to Ambleside
sections.desc: Mostly flat from Elterwater lake down to Skelwith Force (can portage river left). From there are occasional rapids down to Brathay Pool. It is possible to takeout here, or carry on down to the confluence with the Rothay and onto Windermere, heading across the lake to takeout at the pier.
sections.directions: Lots of possible put-ins, or indeed paddle straight onto this run from Great Langdale Beck. The putin marked is at the carpark at the road bridge over Great Langdale Beck at Elterwater village. Alternatively find somewhere to putin at the lake, or below Skelwith Falls. Takeout at the pier on Windermere Lake, just outside Ambleside.

sections.name: Calder (Yorkshire) — Sowerby Bridge Whitewater Course
sections.desc: A 300m section of the Calder which has been modified to provide a good introduction to white water, play boating or slalom practice. Maintained by Halifax Canoe Club - contact them for further details.
sections.directions: Halifax CC are located in Greenups Mill in the centre of Sowerby Bridge, near Halifax. From the bridge over the river you can see the put-in and the course. Parking within the mill complex is for residents only, there is a big car park at the rear of B&M supermaket next to the canal. You can drop your boat at the club, but to avoid any problems with residents move your car as soon as you have unloaded.

sections.name: Calder — Thornholme Farm to Calder Bridge
sections.desc: Enjoyable bimble through pleasant countryside, beware of the occasional tree. The whitewater interest lies in the second half of the run where a few rapids liven up the approach to Calder Bridge. It is possible to continue past Calder Bridge, taking in some unusual sandstone gorges. Possible takeouts are a) at a public footpath which goes down to the river, or b) continuing through the Sellafield nuclear site down to the sea. Note that there are a couple of grade 4 rapids through Sellafield which are made all the more interesting by their unique location.
sections.directions: Thornholme Farm can be reached from Calder Bridge by turning off the Cold Fell road as it zig-zags up a steep hill. There isn't much parking, but make sure to leave access for farm traffic. There is a large car park on your left as the Cold Fell road enters Calder Bridge.

sections.name: Caldew — Grainsgill beck to Mosedale
sections.desc: Relentless fun grade 3 with drops of 4 for the first ~1km especially in high water. Eases to grade 2/3 for the latter ~2km. It is possible to put in higher up if you want a warm up, you'll need to walk for it though.
sections.directions: From Mosedale bridge, head north a matter of metres, before taking a left up the small road towards Swineside. There is a reasonable parking area at the put-in near Grainsgill Beck, but be careful if your car doesn't have much ground clearance!

sections.name: Carron (Easter Ross)
sections.notes: High did start at 1.5 now starts at 1.4. Dec 2024.

sections.name: Carron (Easter Ross) (Top)
sections.notes: This top section is not in the Paddle Scotland guidebook. See UKRGB or whitewater.guide. Starts on the Alladale

sections.name: Carron (Wester Ross)
sections.notes: New calibrations Nov 2018, thanks Chris and Gavin

sections.name: Clough — Bellow End Road Bridge to Sedbergh
sections.desc: Lovely run with plenty of interest at the grade. One cheeky hole in particular has been known to catch a few people unawares. A weir about 1/2 way down is runnable, but worth keeping an eye out for as can be retentive at bigger levels.
sections.directions: If driving upstream from the takeout in Sedbergh, put in at the first bridge the A684 crosses the river. The takeout if about 1km after the confluence with the Rawthey, on river right just below the A684 bridge just east of Sedbergh.

sections.name: Clough — Garsdale Head to Bellow End Bridge
sections.desc: Steep and continuous with regular bedrock falls including the infamous Lemmings drop which is notoriously difficult to stop in time to inspect.
sections.directions: Putin at on of the many A684 bridges near Garsdale Station if there is enough water (it's obvious just by looking at the river, what you see is what you get). The section is best combined with the lower section of the river.

sections.name: Clyde (Stonebyres)
sections.notes: Crossford to Hazelbank calibration. New calibrations from Robin April 2018, please fill in calibrations form to confirm or adjust.

sections.name: Cocker — Crummock Water to Southwaite Bridge
sections.desc: The difficulty in this section, if any, lies in the first kilometre, where the river is narrower and trees may be an issue. The remainder is flat and meanders through the scenic valley bottom. The occasional fence may be lurking in the lower section.
sections.directions: The put-in is from the carpark on river right, just upstream of the roadbridge. For the takeout, river left above Southwaite Bridge is the best option, not far from a small parking area.

sections.name: Cocker — Southwaite Bridge to Cockermouth
sections.desc: Often paddled in conjunction with the top section, this part of the river conveniently contains all the whitewater interest if you're after a quick blast down a shorter section. The run starts with a small weir - beware the towback in high levels. The best section of this run is the final kilometre through the town, where the river yields a number of bouncy grade 3's with nice surf waves at certain levels.
sections.directions: Parking is possible on river left above the roadbridge, adjacent to the weir. Take-out just after the confluence from the Derwent, river right just after the first bridge you pass under. There is a huge car park next to a play area where you can leave your car.

sections.name: Coquet — Blindburn to Low Alwinton
sections.desc: A spate run with a few harder falls and rapids near the source.
sections.directions: Follow the road from Alnwinton up into the Cheviots. The road follows the river and water levels will dictate how far up you drive before putting on, with Blindburn being the highest point. Get out at the bridge in Low Alnwinton.

sections.name: Coquet — Low Alwinton to Rothbury
sections.desc: Fast flowing to begin with, before slowing down to touring pace as the river plateaus in the flood plains.
sections.directions: Put in off the road bridge in Low Alnwinton and get out at the bridge in Rothbury. Thropton Bridge may be used as a put-in for a shorter trip.

sections.name: Coquet — Rothbury to Weldon Mill
sections.desc: Fairly fast grade two with the odd grade three rapid.

sections.name: Crake — Blawith Common to Spark Bridge
sections.desc: Fun grade 2/3: builds up in excitement culminating in Bobbin Mill Rapid just before Spark Bridge.
sections.directions: Putin at the south end of Coniston Water. There are a few lay-bys on the west side from where you can walk down to the water's edge. Takeout river right just downstream of the bridge in Spark Bridge.

sections.name: Cray Gill — Cray to Hubberholme
sections.desc: Described by the few who have run it as Yorkshire's best beck. Short and very steep, plenty of falls packed in, some with shallow landings. Needs lots of water, so rarely run.
sections.directions: Either put-in above the big fall in Cray village, or in very high water continue up the road to where the Gill crosses the road again and put on below here.

sections.name: Cree
sections.notes: New calibrations Dec 2025 thanks to Jon.

sections.name: Cuileig (Upper)
sections.notes: New calibrations Oct 2021. Notoriously unreliable gauge, water level often higher than predicted due to large trib joining just below the loch.

sections.name: Dane — Gradbach to Rushton Spencer
sections.desc: Spate river with nice continuous grade 3/4 gorge at the start.

sections.name: Dart — Loop
sections.desc: Hugely popular classic grade 2/3 often used to introduce beginners to whitewater.
sections.directions: Putin at the National Park car park at Newbridge. Take out at the River Dart Country Park.

sections.name: Dart — Upper, Dartmeet to Newbridge
sections.desc: Fabulous grade 4 classic: continuous and isolated away from the road. Highlights in order of appearance are the "mad mile" (full-on in spate), Euthanasia Falls (slidey drop on a RH bend) and "Surprise Surprise!" (an awkward slot).
sections.directions: Takeout at the National Park carpark at Newbridge. Putin at the carpark at Dartmeet.

sections.name: Dee (Grampian) (Garthdee)
sections.notes: Marathon site. Based on 1 calibration, please fill in form to report more

sections.name: Dee (Grampian) (Middle)
sections.notes: Please send calibrations for Woodend gauge for paddling at Potarch. See access link for tree at Invercauld Bridge.

sections.name: Dee (Grampian) (Top)
sections.notes: Please send calibrations for this section on with Mar Lodge gauge

sections.name: Derwent (Derbyshire) — Darley Dale to Matlock
sections.desc: Mostly gentle paddle, with a few bits of continuous grade 2, including the slalom site near the take-out.

sections.name: Deveron
sections.notes: New calibrations 31-03-2019. Please send more reports for confirmation or correction. This is a long river and calibrations will differ depending on section run.

sections.name: Divie
sections.notes: Please send calibrations for confirmation

sections.name: Don — Stocksbridge to Oughtibridge
sections.desc: Starts off flat with the odd grade 2, then a good play wave followed by a bouldery grade 3 section.
sections.directions: Putin at the bridge near the museum between Deepcar and Thurgoland. Take out at the road bridge in Oughtibridge. There are mixed messages on this but Sheffield Canoe Club's site is nearby and often suggested as an egress: however their car park is usually locked so unless you are a member I think it's best to use the road bridge. An alternative is to extend the trip by 2km and continue to takeout at SK328916 (where the blue P&R letters are on the map).

sections.name: Douglas — Red Rock Lane to Flood Prevention Barrage
sections.desc: Shallow urban stream running from Worthington Lakes reservoir down towards Wigan town centre. Despite it's proximity to urban sprawl, it's not as built up as you'd think once you're down at river level. The river keeps a fairly rapid flow throughout, although it never gets above grade 2. Beware of fallen trees and branches.
sections.directions: Follow the A49 north out of wigan, turning right onto the A5106 at a roundabout with an Esso garage. After ~1km, turn right onto Red-Rock Lane (B5239) at a mini-roundabout and you cross the river immediately. There is very limited parking here, but ~200m up the hill is a free car park. To find the take-out, retrace your steps back onto the A49, turn left Coppull Lane, and drive down to the river. There's plenty of parking here, but leave space at the bottom for other cars to turn round.

sections.name: Duddon — Birk's Bridge to Hall Dunnerdale
sections.desc: An absolute classic. At the put-in is the gun-barrel run (gd5) - 100m of narrow siphon-filled mank for the brave. 500m of gd3 leads into Troutal gorge (gd5): portage river left. Fun, continuous grade 3 water leads down to Wallowbarrow gorge (continuous gd4+/5), inspect along the footpath on river right. The river then eases off for the last 2km down to Hall Bridge.
sections.directions: Takeout at Hall Dunnerdale Bridge to the north of Broughton in Furness. To reach the putin head upstream to a picnic site by the river at Birks bridge (a disused bridge just off the road).

sections.name: Duddon — Ulpha to Duddon Bridge
sections.desc: Fun grade 3 run with a couple of challenges. A large island warns of the lead-in to Rawford bridge (gd4), which is followed by a nasty weir.
sections.directions: Putin at the bridge just south of Ulpha or continue from the section above. Takeout immediately downstream of Duddon Bridge on the river left.

sections.name: Dye
sections.notes: Added Nov 2018. Please report calibrations to confirm or adjust. Gauge and webcam link is on Feuch.

sections.name: Eamont — Waterfoot to Brougham Castle
sections.desc: Popular open boat trip, with the occasional weir to add spice!
sections.directions: Takeout just above the weir at Brougham Castle and follow the public footpath to the lay-by just off the A66

sections.name: Earn
sections.notes: Please send calibrations. Reports are: 0.75 high, 1 vhigh.

sections.name: East Allen — Sinderhope to Allen Confluence
sections.desc: A fairly continuous spate beck, with one 3m fall.
sections.directions: In spate conditions the river is runnable from Sinderhope Ford. Get out either at Thornley Gate Bridge just outside of Allendale Town, or continue to Cupola Bridge on the Allen.

sections.name: East Lyn — Brendon to Watersmeet
sections.desc: Fun continuous boulder rapids and drops. Hardest drop is a two-tier waterfall about halfway down.
sections.directions: Putin at the village of Brendon. Please be considerate and change before you get there. Although it is possible to takeout at Watermeets, you'd be mad not to continue straight onto the section downstream and takeout at the sea.

sections.name: East Lyn — Watersmeet to the Sea
sections.desc: Excellent creeking run, with most of the action in one long gorge.
sections.directions: Takeout in Lynmouth where the river enters the sea. Putin at Watermeet at the confluence with the Hoaroak: park on the A39 and carry down to the river.

sections.name: Eden (Lakes) — Lazonby to Armathwaite
sections.desc: Flat sections interspersed by grade 2/3 rapids - enough of a gap to pick up the pieces if it all goes to pot. A great first taste of whitewater. Armathwaite weir is easily portageable on river left if needs be.
sections.directions: A large car-park on river left just upstream of the bridge at Lazonby provides an ideal put-in, with steps down to the river. Takeout river right just below the bridge at Armathwaite.

sections.name: Ehen — Wath Brow Bridge to Low Mill
sections.desc: The river is a pleasant run through fields and a couple of villages. The gradient remains fairly consistent throughout keeping interest all the way. A couple of weirs in Egremont can be easily shot and only become nasty in the highest of water levels, when both can be portaged. Downstream of Egremont, a small broken weir can form a nice play-wave, getting really good at levels between 1.5 and 2m. Those wanting to extend the trip can continue on down to Braystones (or even to the Sellafield site), though the river is easier on this section.
sections.directions: For the put-in, park in the large parking area just downstream and river right of the picturesque Wath Brow bridge. Drive southwards past Egremont, taking your first right after Thornhill to reach the take-out. Parking here is more limited.

sections.name: Ericht (Blairgowrie)
sections.notes: Contact river advisor Mary Conacher mary.conacher5@btinternet.com for gate code. Huge was 1.7 now 1.8 Feb 2020.

sections.name: Erme — Harford Bridge to Ivybridge
sections.desc: Classic narrow creeking. At high water watch out for the slot just downstream of a series of small ledges (~2km in). The run cranks up from here, culminating in the Erme gorge which starts under the railway viaduct. Inspect along the path on river right. Takeout at the footbridge in Ivybridge. Below about 0.63 on the gauge, it is recommended to park in Ivybridge and walk-in to the slot rapid, as above here starts to get scrapy.
sections.directions: Takeout at the footbridge in the centre of Ivybridge where there is plenty of parking. Putin at the road bridge at Harford, a small village north of Ivybridge.

sections.name: Esk (Lakes) — Brotherikeld to Forge Bridge
sections.desc: Fun classic section of the Esk: no nasties but watch out for trees.
sections.directions: Park at the layby at the bottom of Hardknott Pass next to the track up to Brotherilkeld farm. Walk up the track towards the farm and take the footpath down to the river. Takeout at Forge Bridge, near Eskdale Green village.

sections.name: Esk (Yorkshire) — Egton Bridge to Whitby
sections.desc: Mostly a grade 2 bimble with a couple of weirs and the option to paddle out to sea at the end!
sections.directions: Put in at Egton Bridge and take out at Whitby Harbour.

sections.name: Esk (Yorkshire) — Houlsyke to Egton Bridge
sections.desc: An expedition into the Yorkshire Moors in heavy rain may result in finding this river up. It consists of three gorges running at grade 3 (possibly 4 in high levels) connected by flat water.
sections.directions: It is possible to put in at Castleton, but this only adds another 10km of arduous flat water. The normal put-in is therefore a mile or two above Lealholm, under a railway bridge and along a footpath across a field. Parking here is difficult, we dropped the boats and parked in a layby a few hundred metres further up the road on the left. Get out river right at Egton Bridge.

sections.name: Etive (Middle)
sections.notes: Experimental Calibration based on a gauge on a river to the south east of Etive catchment (on a different river). Variability between the two rivers exists but in general they respond similarly to rain as they have broadly similar catchment areas and topography. Localised rainfall differences particularly summer thunderstorms may result in significant differences in level. As with any river you should satisfy yourself that the level is sutible for you and your group when you get there. Please send in more calibrations.

sections.notes: Access link added Jan 2024 with tree blockage

sections.name: Ettrick (Upper)
sections.notes: Not many calibrations for higher levels, please send more

sections.name: Evan Water
sections.notes: New July 2020. Needs calibrations for scrape and low.

sections.notes: Feb 2020 recalibration Huge 1.3→1.4, VHigh 1.2→1.3

sections.name: Feshie
sections.notes: Calibrations updated Dec 2023. Reported to be empty at 0.6. Main run is rarely done so probably needs more water.

sections.name: Findhorn (Gorge) (New Gauge)
sections.notes: New Logie Bridge gauge closer to section. 0.37 reported as low. More calibrations needed.

sections.notes: New Access Issue tree discussion Dec 2023

sections.notes: New gauge Nov 2019, more calibrations needed

sections.name: Findhorn (Upper)
sections.notes: New Access Issue Feb 2019

sections.name: Gala Water
sections.notes: 0.764 on Galashiels gauge reported as high

sections.name: Garbh Uisge (Leny)
sections.notes: Access issue added 9 Dec 2021 see link

sections.name: Garry (Perthshire)
sections.notes: New gauge Nov 2019, more calibrations needed

sections.name: Garry (Perthshire) (Calvine)
sections.notes: Needs calibrations for Dalnamein. Water compensation flow is new since 2019 so not many paddlers. See this discussion.

sections.name: Gelt — Binney Bank to Low Gelt Bridge
sections.desc: Run of continued interest through some narrow gorges with the spicy combination of sparse eddies and a high risk of trees to keep you on your toes.
sections.directions: Put in at Binney Bank, or if you don't value your warm-up opportunities, hop in at Hynam Bridge to drop straight into the thick of it. Take out at Low Geltbridge, just off the A69.

sections.name: Girvan
sections.notes: Data seems wrong March 2026

sections.name: Goyt — Brabyn's Park to MCC site
sections.desc: A collection of weirs coupled with MCC's slalom site. Possible to extend the trip with more weirs in high water by starting as far up as Whalley Bridge or getting out as far down as Stockport. In spate some weirs will need portaging.

sections.name: Green Field Beck — Low Green Field to Beckermonds
sections.desc: Small spate stream which joins Oughtershaw Beck to form the Wharfe. Narrow and quite continuos - look out for fences and a surprise small fall on a bend. Worth doing as a warm up for the Upper Wharfe in high water.
sections.directions: Drive past the farmyard at the get-in for the Upper Wharfe in Beckmonds. You'll need to open a couple of gates on the road. When you see a forestry track on the right, park here and walk down to the river on the left. It may be paddleable higher up in spate, but the road is private above this point making access tricky.

sections.name: Greta (Keswick) — Threlkeld to Keswick
sections.desc: A popular grade 3 classic. That this is one of the few UK rivers with a sensible access agreement. Paddling is permitted year round, but in Nov-Dec the level must be above the white marker on the bridge to avoid damaging salmon spawning redds. Whilst the white line may possibly be positioned a bit high, it corresponds to a level of approx 1.41m on the Low Briery Gauge. The river itself changed considerably in the December 2015 floods, but is still a classic, even if some rapids have been lost and new ones formed.
sections.directions: Putin at Threlkeld bridge, along a small road off the A66 just east of Threlkeld (signposted to the Youth Centre and Castlerigg Stone Circle). Takeout on river right at the climbing wall carpark in Keswick. Alternatively paddle another flatish 1.5km down to onto the Derwent and takeout on river right just before the suspension footbridge at Portinscale.

sections.name: Greta (Tees) — Gilmonby Bridge to Rutherford Bridge
sections.desc: An extra few kms to add to the start of the Greta at a slightly easier grade to the rest. The weir above Rutherford Bridge can be dodgy in high water.
sections.directions: Put-in from the footpath at Gilmonby Bridge, down the road from Bowes (easier to park in Bowes and walk down the hill). Walking a few hundred metres upstream will allow you to run Mill Force (3+) as a warm up. You can take out at Rutherford Bridge, but would be better to continue on down the next section.

sections.name: Greta (Tees) — Rutherford to Tees Confluence
sections.desc: Good continuous grade 3 run that ends with 100m of grade 4 just above the confluence with the Tees. The final stretch (including Rokesby falls) is difficult to inspect/portage, so be prepared to read and run.
sections.directions: Putin at the bridge in Rutherford. Takeout after the confluence with the Tees: the first available takeout is river left just above Whorlton Lido (clamber up the steep bank), or continue on the Tees down to Winston Bridge as it will be at a fun level if the Greta is running.

sections.name: Gryfe
sections.notes: Low changed 0.4→0.45 Feb 2020

sections.name: Hebden Water — Black Dean to Hebden Bridge
sections.desc: Continuous grade three boulder garden spate beck through a wooded valley in West Yorkshire.
sections.directions: Put in at Black Dean road bridge, take out in Hebden Water.

sections.name: Hindburn — Millbeck to Wray
sections.desc: Great run: steep slabs at the start, plenty of grade 3 and then a straightforward but bigger fall towards the end. Beware of this one in bigger levels as there aren't many eddies above it!
sections.directions: Takeout at Mealbank bridge, on the B6480 just north of Wray. Putin at the bridge near Lowgill village: go across the first bridge across the Hindburn and 100m later is another bridge over a small side beck at a sharp bend: from here there is access down to the confluence.

sections.name: Holme — Sands to Magdale
sections.desc: The Holme is rarely paddled – probably due to the scarcity of a decent amount of water. However, if deep enough, it offers a picturesque paddle with a frequent variety of features. Its course is heavily wooded for the most part and you will be unaware that in some sections you are passing through a small town. The occasional bankside mill and the number of weirs give a clue to the industrial past of the area. At lower levels, some parts can be a little ‘scrapey’ but the most notable and enjoyable features are the rapids which occur in several short sections. The best of these is at Smithy Plac
sections.directions: Sands playing fields are on the outskirts of Holmfirth next to Holmfirth Swimming Baths on the A6024. There is a large free car park right next to the river here. However, this may be busy on winter Sunday mornings due to the adjacent football pitches. The adventurous can put in above the footbridge and tackle the almost immediate 1.7m vertical drop. For the more sedate, (and those of us who have noticed shopping trolleys in the weir before now, ) it is very easy to cross the footbridge, walk a few metres downstream and put in in the adjacent woodland. Look out for the Herons which often feed

sections.name: Idle — Ordsall to Retford
sections.desc: Perfect intro to moving water for beginners. Gently moving flat water with a couple of small weirs which allow for an intro to playing. Can easily be extended by continuing on to one of the bridges downstream.
sections.directions: Put-in river left on Goosemore Lane. Shuttle up the A638, turning off immediately after you turn left onto the A620. Park in the large car park next to the river.

sections.name: Irthing — Crammel Linn to Gilsland
sections.desc: Huge waterfall (Crammel Linn) at the start, get in above or below depending on skill and bravery levels! Rest of the run is grade 3 with sloping weirs. Higher water brings
sections.directions: Put in at the waterfall after driving along the single track road and walking down the boggy path. Get out at the stepping stones above the village of Gilsland.

sections.name: Irwell — Ramsbottom to the Burrs
sections.desc: The full run from Ramsbottom contains a collection of weirs to shoot. The Burrs site itself has been developed for paddlers, with a collection of playable waves and stoppers. Careful of the big weir at the top of the Burrs site in high water. The stopper can become nasty.
sections.directions: The put-in from Ramsbottom is upstream of the main road bridge. The Burrs site itself can be used as a take-out, or a base to do laps.

sections.name: Kelvin
sections.notes: Access issue added 16 Feb 2020

sections.name: Kent — Kentmere to Scroggs Bridge
sections.desc: The first 200m is fairly tree ridden and may be worth portaging if super high. The exit to Kentmere Tarn can also be a bit tree-eey but the flow isn't fast so portaging is OK. The remainder of the run is constantly moving so provides continual interest throughout. The highlight is a few hundred metres of grade 3, not far after a pretty mini-gorge. If you don't plan to run the rapid at Scroggs bridge (grade 4), it might be worth scouting your take-out eddy on the way up.
sections.directions: Take the small turning in Staveley signposted to Kentmere. When the road crosses to river left as you head north, you've reached Scroggs Bridge, the takeout. Continue northwards up the valley until you reach Kentmere. Parking here is very limited, so be discrete and try not to block passing places. A gate and small stile give access to the river on river left.

sections.name: Kent — Scroggs Bridge to Burneside
sections.desc: Two grade 4 rapids and four significant weirs. The run starts with a bang at Scroggs Bridge, putting in below is possible if you'd rather a more sedate warm up. A couple of weirs appear through Staveley. The undoubted highlight of the section is the rapid through the Cowan Head complex. A weir drops into a long steep powerful (and really fun) rapid.
sections.directions: Take the small turning in Staveley signposted to Kentmere. When the road crosses to river left as you head north, you've reached Scroggs Bridge, the put-in. Driving south from Staveley, look for signs to the left to Burneside. There's three options so don't worry if you miss the first one. Downstream of the bridge (river right) in Burneside is a small park and area for parking.

sections.name: Kent — Scroggs Weir to Park Head
sections.desc: A classic. Short and sharp with a few falls, finishing with a flourish at Force Falls.
sections.directions: Putin at Scroggs weir which can be reached by heading down a small lane south of Kendal (the first turnoff after the coming off the A591 dual carriageway if you are heading north). Takeout on river right immediately after Force Falls underneath the A591 bridge (exit at the Sedgewick junction and head along the minor roads to the river). If levels are low (below about 0.5) it is better to get in at Prizet Bridge as most of the interest is below this point (and it's mostly scrapey above here at these levels). There is limited parking here though, so you're best leaving most cars at the takeout.

sections.name: Kinnel Water
sections.notes: See access issue link for tree blockage cleared March 2020

sections.name: Kirk Burn
sections.notes: Added June 2020. Thanks to Calum P for calibrations. Flows into Glazert then Kelvin.

sections.name: Leven — Newby Bridge to Low Wood
sections.desc: Excellent short blast, with plenty of playwaves, weirs and rapids. Runs at a variety of levels, often for days after rain as Windermere lake drains. Backbarrow is the main event - an intimidating grade 4 under the road bridge, but with a nice big pool to mop up the pieces! You often have an audience from the hotel. The big weir after Backbarrow can be run at grade 5, but not recommended - there's a simple portage on river left. Current recommendation is to get out river right above the roadbridge at Low Wood to avoid erosion of the bank below the bridge on river left.
sections.directions: The put-in on river right on the small road just downstream of the bridge (in Newby Bridge) is right on some salmon redds. Provided you won't touch/scrape over these as you launch, you'll be fine. If not, find an alternative put-in or perhaps a different river for the day.

sections.name: Liddel Water
sections.notes: Calibrations unconfirmed, please send more to confirm. Beware of trespass into England.

sections.name: Ling
sections.notes: New section Jan 2019. Calibrations based on only 3 readings, please send more.

sections.name: Lochay
sections.notes: Gauge is on Dochart so may be unrelated

sections.name: Lowther — Crookwath Bridge to Brougham Castle
sections.desc: Bouldery grade 2/3 rapids in pleasant woodland.
sections.directions: To put-in, take the public footpath down to the river at Crookwath Bridge. Get out on the right bank above Brougham Castle Bridge. Alternatively, for a shorter run get on at Askham Bridge and get off at the A6 Bridge at the entrance to Lowther Caravan Site.

sections.name: Lugar Water
sections.notes: Not many calibrations 1.0 appears high, 1.65 appears VHigh. Please send more calibrations.

sections.name: Lune — Halton Rapids
sections.desc: A few hundred metres of rapids between two weirs: park-n-play.
sections.directions: Heading east from Lancaster along the A683 take a small left down to the river about 0.5km after passing under the M6. At the bottom of the hill, before crossing the bridge to Halton, park at the Lancaster University boathouse. The putin is reach by walking up the diused railway track on river left, and putting in below the top weir (don't go right up to the weir as it will mess with the fish counter).

sections.name: Lune — Lowgill to Rawthey Confluence
sections.desc: A classic section with easy access. The narrow gorges are still fun in low water and the "The Strid" becomes a monster in epic water. Two weirs after Killington Bridge can be avoided by getting out at Killington Bridge itself - this is recommended if you have inexperienced paddlers in your group.
sections.directions: Putin at the Crook of Lune bridge, along a small road just off the B6257 just south of the M6. There is no parking at the bridge, and the residents have asked that you don't drive down the narrow lane to drop off boats. Park at the end of the lane and carry the boats down to the river - possibly paddling Low Gill on the way. Takeout on river left about 300m downstream of the Rawthey confluence. A bridleway leads up to track back to the road where there is a large layby to park.

sections.name: Lune — Tebay to Lowgill
sections.desc: The rapid under the disused road bridge is by far the hardest on the section. A weir immediately above this rapid gets terminal in high water, but it is possible to put in between the two if you fancy the rapid but not the weir. The river is pretty grade 2 from here on down, making you forget about the roaring motorway in the same valley.
sections.directions: The best put-in is an old road bridge over the river, just to the north of where A685 crosses the M6. Walk upstream on river right to paddle the drop, or downstream on river left to put-in below. To reach the takeout, drive south along the A685 forking left onto the B6257. As you pass under a bridge just south of the M6 there is an old viaduct on your left with a small lane running under it. The takeout is at the bridge just down this lane, however the residents have asked that you don't park at the bridge itself. Park at the end of the lane and walk back to your car... or, carry on downstream

sections.name: Luss Water
sections.notes: March 2020 Low 0.5→0.7, Medium 0.7→0.9, High 0.9→1.0, vhigh 1.0→1.1. Thanks Brenden

sections.name: Lyon
sections.notes: See Access Issue link for road issues Oct 2023.

sections.name: Lyon (Upper)
sections.notes: Needs calibrations during a release

sections.name: Mint — Patton Bridge to Mint Bridge
sections.desc: Sister river to the Sprint, but a fair bit easier. Getting in higher up is possible, but higher water would be required as a minimum and trees tend to be more of a problem.
sections.directions: Takeout at the recycle area of the Morrisons on the A6 just north of Kendal. Putin on river left at Patton Bridge, if there's not enough space to park, try the minor road on the other side of the river which heads off upstream.

sections.name: Moriston
sections.notes: New gauge, please send calibrations

sections.name: Muick
sections.notes: New access signage Oct 2019, see access issue link

sections.name: Nethan
sections.notes: 0.735 reported as VHigh, please send in calibrations

sections.name: Nith (Drumlanrig)
sections.notes: Strainer near end removed, see access issue link

sections.name: North Esk (Lower)
sections.notes: Jan 2026 - Collapsed bridge now in s-bend/shogun, passable at high water, a problem at low water, may move and become worse.

sections.name: North Esk (Lower) (Old)
sections.notes: Old gauge near the sea. Access issue link added July 2024.

sections.name: North Esk (Middle)
sections.notes: New section from Alex Crossland, low and scrape are guesses please send calibrations to confirm. Gauge is called Waterside Perth and is below Tarfside confluence.

sections.name: North Esk (Upper) (Invermark Gauge)
sections.notes: New Invermark gauge Oct 2023, please send more calibrations, currently it only has High calibrated.

sections.name: Oughtershaw Beck — Oughtershaw to Beckermonds
sections.desc: Combines with Green Field Beck to form the Upper Wharfe. Spate tree and fence filled steep ditch with plenty of tight rapids and small falls.
sections.directions: Walk up the footpath above Oughtershaw village and put-on wherever looks sensible.

sections.name: Ouse Burn — South Gosforth to Heaton
sections.desc: Random urban spate boating in the middle of Geordie land. A few weirs and one 4m waterfall. You must get out before Heaton as the river disappears underground!
sections.directions: Put in and take out wherever suits around Jesmond Park. Highest point is South Gosforth, absolutely must get out before Heaton, Armstrong bridge probably the best bet.

sections.name: Ouse — Linton Weir
sections.desc: Popular play spot consisting of a fish ladder and 3m weir. At certain levels a play wave is formed.

sections.name: Plym — Cadover Bridge to Shaugh Bridge
sections.desc: Excellent, but challenging run: starts with a series of pool-drop rapids, then gets steeper and more continuous.
sections.directions: Putin at Cadover bridge on the minor roads south-east of Yelverton. Takeout at Shaugh bridge, just west of the village of Shaugh Prior, or continue straight onto the section downstream.

sections.name: Plym — Shaugh Bridge to Bickleigh Bridge
sections.desc: Starts with a bang, then eases to pool-drop. Takeout on river right at a beach 200m above Bickleigh Bridge (residents prefer it).
sections.directions: Takeout at the bridge near Bickleigh village. Putin at the bridge just west of Shaugh Prior.

sections.name: Rawthey — Rawthey Bridge to Sedbergh
sections.desc: Fantastic run: continuous grade 3 dotted with a few garder bedrock falls.
sections.directions: Putin at Rawthey Bridge: head out of Sedburgh through Cautley along the A683, and the bridge is about 2km north of Cross Keys. Takeout on river right at the A683 bridge just north of Sedburgh, or continue onto the next section.

sections.name: Rawthey — Sedbergh to Lune Confluence
sections.desc: An addition to the main Rawthey section, consists of a few weirs and one rapid of note near the end - railway falls(IV).
sections.directions: If you're not just running this as an add-on to the last section, then put on at Sedbergh New Bridge where there's a big lay-by and a path to the river. Best get-out is on the Lune, 500m below the confluence where there's a bridleway on river left.

sections.name: Ribble — Clitheroe to Ribchester
sections.desc: Good touring run, with just 1 weir to watch out for.
sections.directions: Putin at Edisford Road Bridge, just west of Clitheroe. Takeout at Ribchester School.

sections.name: Ribble — Helwith Bridge to Settle
sections.desc: After about 1km a footbridge marks the run into "Twin Bridges", a long rapid under two railway bridges. Further downstream stop on river right just after a small stone bridge to inspect Stainforth Force, a tricky 3-tier drop. Can be portaged on river right. From here down to Settle is pleasant grade 3 but watch out for 2 weirs, both a bit sketchy.
sections.directions: Putin at Helwith Bridge, there is a picnic area on river right. Takeout on river right just after a footbridge below "Queen's Rock", the last significant rapid in Settle (about 100m below the main road bridge). Carry back over the footbridge to river left out to Kings Mill housing estate.

sections.name: Roeburn — Barkin Bridge to Wray
sections.desc: Continuous grade 3 run, with one fall in a gorge reaching grade 4 in high water which is awkward to portage. The gorge starts just after a small footbridge, and is best inspected by clambering along the left bank: the 2m drop at the end is sticky in high water.
sections.directions: Putin at Barkin Bridge: from Wray follow the minor road towards High Salter (marked Roeburndale West). Follwo this road to where it crosses the river. There is only space for 1 car by the bridge. Takeout on river left just below the road bridge on the east side of Wray. Alternatively continue past the confluence with the Hindburn to the carpark by the weir just to the north of Wray.

sections.name: Rookhope Burn — Footbridge to Eastgate
sections.desc: Rarely paddled spate ditch Wear trib with a few waterfalls including a 4-5m fall which looks quite photogenic. Get out at Eastgate Bridge or continue onto the Wear.

sections.name: Rothay — Grassmere to Lake Windermere
sections.desc: Gentle low grade paddle in the central Lakes encompassing Grassmere Lake and Rydal Water.
sections.directions: Put-in either on Grassmere Lake or on the river above. Take out at the final weir or on Lake Windermere.

sections.name: Rye — Hawnby to Helmsley
sections.desc: Set in the steep wooded Rye valley, flows fast off the Yorkshire moors after recent rain. Beware of the tree lined banks in high water.
sections.directions: Put in at the road bridge in Hawnby and get off in Helmsley. Flat below here until the Derwent.

sections.name: Scalby Beck — Mowthorpe Farm to Sea
sections.desc: An odd man-made river, mostly flat, but loads of weirs to shoot, some of which can be tricky.

sections.name: Scaur Water
sections.notes: Also called Scar Water. Low 0.9→0.89 Feb 2020.

sections.name: Severn — Shrewsbury Weir
sections.desc: Shrewsbury Weir is a playspot that comes into condition only when the Severn is very high. At lower levels it can form a dangerous stopper and should be avoided - note that the level suggested here is only an indicator that it should be running. If it looks nasty, it probably is - don't get on! The wave flushes when the river rises further.
sections.directions: The weir is just downstream of the town centre itself. There is ample parking along Sydney Avenue - just find somewhere the water won't be start lapping at your car whilst you're strutting your stuff.

sections.name: Snizort
sections.notes: Guidebook says 1.25 needed on gauge but bank inspection at 0.8 looked low but paddleable at start (photo). More calibrations welcome.

sections.name: South Esk (Angus)
sections.notes: New access issue April 2024

sections.name: South Tyne — Alston to Slaggyford
sections.desc: An easy spate run, popular with open boaters.
sections.directions: Putin at Alston, parking near the tourist railway. Takeout at Slaggyford where a small road bridge crosses the river. It is possible to extend the run in various ways, even paddling 24km all the way down to Haltwhistle.

sections.name: South Tyne — Garrigill to Alston
sections.desc: A high water trip starting at grade 3 and dropping back to grade 2.

sections.name: South Tyne — Tynehead to Garrigill
sections.desc: Paddling near the source of the South Tyne. This spate section is small and narrow, containing several gorges and is quite continuous in nature.
sections.directions: Drive up the Tyne head road from Garrigill, until you reach a gated track. Walk down to the river here. Get out at the bridge in Garrigill or combine with the section to Alston.

sections.name: Spean (Gorge)
sections.notes: Gauge is not on this river and often does not reflect well the flow here. See Access Issue link for tree stuck Sept 2023

sections.name: Spey
sections.notes: Ayeon pool access now improved. New access issue at Fochabers, see link below.

sections.name: Sprint — Public Toilet to Sprint Bridge
sections.desc: A Cumbrian classic. Small and fast with numerous bedrock falls and rapids.
sections.directions: Takeout at the bridge just east of Burneside. To reach the putin head upstream through Garnett Bridge to the public toilets just north of Yewbarrow Hall.

sections.name: Spurlswood Beck — Woodland Fell to Bedburn Beck Source
sections.desc: Spate ditch in Hamsterley Forest. Mostly grade 2/3 but with one large fall (Blackling Hole) which can be run just as a park-and-huck in lower levels than needed for the rest of the beck.
sections.directions: Use the Forest Drive in Hamsterley after paying the £3 toll. Park at Blackling Hole and walk up as high as you can be bothered. Take out at the car park near the Grove or carry on down Bedburn Beck.

sections.name: Stonesdale Beck — Stonesdale Lane Bridge to Swale Confluence
sections.desc: Small, steep trib of the Upper Swale with plenty of small drops, fences and a short walled-in gorge containing some siphons near the end. Finishes with Currack Force waterfall which has a very shallow landing in all but spate levels. Thanks to Dave Peel for info.
sections.directions: In high water put-in at road bridge on Stonesdale Lane when driving towards Tan Hill. Also possible to put in from bridleway about 1km further down the valley with a short walk-in. Either take-out above Currack Force or carry on down the Swale where it merges just below Rainby Force (although easy to get out and run Rainby too).

sections.name: Swale — Grinton to Richmond
sections.desc: Mellow touring run through beautiful countryside.
sections.directions: Putin at Grinton bridge. Takeout in Richmond, at the carpark on river left downstream of the bridge.

sections.name: Swale — Hoggarths to Ivelet Bridge
sections.desc: Classic waterfall run. Wain Wath Force is the first drop, obvious from the road on the drive up to the putin. The drops get bigger: Rainby Force, then the only real 'rapid' rather than fall, the double drop of Catrake Force, a short easy gorge section then Upper and Lower Kisdon (the last and most serious).
sections.directions: If there is decent levels putin at the Hoggarths road bridge upstream of Keld, and takeout at small bridge on the way to Ivelet (just downstream of Muker). This gives a gentle warm-up and -down either side of the falls. If the water levels are low the falls still go, but the start and end will be barely paddleable. In these conditions it is best to get-on just above Wain Wath falls (visible from the road), and take-out at Lower Kisdon on river right, carrying the km back upstream to Keld via the footpath.

sections.name: Swale — Richmond to Catterick Bridge
sections.desc: Pleasant low grade intro to white water, good for open boats too. Richmond falls can be run at the put-in at grade 4 and there's often a playwave at the Catterick Bridge get-out.
sections.directions: Put-in by Richmond falls, or the bridge downstream near the station. Get out at Catterick Bridge after passing under the A1.

sections.name: Tarff
sections.notes: New calibrations 19 April 2019. Thanks Jack!

sections.name: Tavy — Tavistock to Denham Bridge
sections.desc: A quieter version of the Dart Loop. Mostly grade two, with one notable grade three after the Walkham confluence.

sections.name: Tay (Kenmore)
sections.notes: See Access link for issue at Chinese bridge

sections.name: Tay (Stanley)
sections.notes: Parking for Paddle Scotland members only, get code (changed Aug 2021) from Access Issue link below

sections.name: Tees — Barnard Castle to Winston Bridge
sections.desc: Classic lower section of the Tees. Fun grade 3 trip, an excellent playrun at medium-high levels. Highlights are Abbey rapids (river narrows into a mini-gorge) and Whorlton Lido (a river-wide reef).
sections.directions: Putin at Barnard Castle: park in the visitors car-park for the young offenders institute and walk down to the river getting on just above the weir. Takeout at Winston bridge (a path leads up from river right just upstream of the bridge). In low levels, the section from Whorlton to Winston may not be worth it, get out at Whorlton using the footpath river left just above the falls. In very low levels, Abbey rapids will still work as a park and play spot, either using the verge on river right above the road bridge, or parking at the Abbey itself.

sections.name: Tees — Cotherstone to Barnard Castle
sections.desc: Gentle section of the Tees which runs when other sections are too low, or combined with them to make for a longer trip. A couple of surf waves help to maintain the interest.
sections.directions: Put on where the Balder joins the Tees. Plenty of parking down a small lane in Cotherstone, sign posted "to the river." Take out either above the big weir before Barnard Castle, using HMYO car park, or at various points in BC or combine with Abbey Rapids for an exciting finish.

sections.name: Tees — High Force to Scooberry Bridge
sections.desc: Classic upper section of the Tees. Ledge drop in nature with two larger rapids: "Dog Leg" and "Low Force". Remains fun at low levels, making it a popular run.
sections.directions: Putin at the High Force Hotel, using the footpath just downstream of the footpath to High Force itself. The hotel may try to charge you for access, a contentious issue. To avoid this, there is a car park 600m downstream at the junction with the road up Ettersgill Beck. Takeout either at Wynch Bridge just downstream of Low Force, or continue down to Scooberry Bridge near Newbiggin.

sections.name: Tees — Middleton Bridge to Cotherstone
sections.desc: Best when the river is in flood, but remains paddleable at low levels. Flat down to Eggleston Bridge, followed by bouncy grade 3.
sections.directions: Putin at Middleton bridge. Takeout at Cotherstone, head along the track beside the Balder to the river, the turning is easy to miss. It is possible to extend and takeout in Barnard Castle itself.

sections.name: Teme — Ludlow to Ashford Carbonell
sections.desc: Relaxing bimble with a few weirs.

sections.name: Teviot
sections.notes: Webcam link is near Kelso.

sections.name: Tilt (Marble Lodge)
sections.notes: See access issue for trees reported Oct 2023

sections.name: Trent — Sawley Weir
sections.desc: A big wave river left, and at certain levels a hole river right that can be played on all day, each working best at different levels (once you've worked out how to get on them).
sections.directions: It is possible to park briefly just off the road at the canal cut, to unload, sort kit etc. There is normally ample parking just up the road in Sawley. Put onto the cut above the flood lock and paddle a couple of hundred metres to the junction with the river. Nip past the buoys on the right, and have some fun. Getting back, simply take out, put back in on the cut on paddle back to the start. It's also possible, with arrangement, to park at the Hartington Arms pub and walk across the field at the back to the river. But this involves a long carry and an uphill paddle to get to the wave.

sections.name: Trent — Trent Lock (Thrumpton Weir)
sections.desc: A big green (brown) fast wave that you can front surf and carve around on to your hearts content. The shape of the waves favours longer (faster) boats.
sections.directions: The best parking spot (i.e. the one that causes least bother to locals) is the public car parks near the Trent Lock Inn. Once on the water, paddle downstream ~300m, avoid turning left onto the canal. Just after the railway bridge is the weir - it’s possible to paddle past the bouys on the left. Getting back you have two choices - put in above the weir and paddle upstream, which can be a challenge in high flows / wind, or paddle downstream a few hundred meters and turn left to come back along the canal cut, portaging the lock.

sections.name: Tummel (Bottom)
sections.notes: New calibrations added Oct 2023. I need reports still for Scrape High, V High, currently the calibrations are guesses.

sections.name: Tweed (Berwick)
sections.notes: Access issue at Melrose Cauld added June 2020. Old gauge near the sea but calibrated for Fairnilee.

sections.name: Tweed (Fairnilee)
sections.notes: Access issue at Melroe Cauld added June 2020. New calibrations Feb 2020, please send more calibrations for this Peebles gauge as relevant for Fairnilee

sections.name: Tweed (Makerstoun)
sections.notes: Please send calibrations for this Boleside gauge as relevant for Makerstoun

sections.name: Upper Meig
sections.notes: New calibrations 2021-10-31. Gauge is for Upper section. Lower Section is below a dam and always has some flow. Upper Upper needs recent rain.

sections.name: Ure — Aysgarth Falls
sections.desc: A series of three difficult falls, runnable in high water.
sections.directions: Park in the car park on the northern bank and walk down to the road and onto the footpath back upstream for the first fall. Get out river left after the final fall and follow the footpaths back to the car park.

sections.name: Ure — Aysgarth Falls to Wensley Bridge
sections.desc: Fun grade 3 run from the bottom of Aysgarth Falls. The river is more potent in the first half until Redmire force, which in higher water can reach grade 5, so inspection may be necessary.
sections.directions: Park in the National Trust carpark and follow the footpath to putin just below the falls. Egress at the main road bridge in Wensley.

sections.name: Ure — Masham to Slenningford Water Mill
sections.desc: A classic introduction to whitewater with Hack Falls and Slenningford Rapids being the highlights. Care should be taken at a number of weirs, in particular Tanfield wier just before Slenningford Rapids
sections.directions: There are several options for the put-in: the most hassle-free is to park at the public car park above Hack Falls and access via the public footpath; Mickley village if you want to avoid Hack Falls; or from Masham for a longer run. Takeout at Slenningford Water Mill, which has a shop, toilets and changing area and may require payment for use of the facilities.

sections.name: Ure — Slenningford Water Mill
sections.desc: Well maintained site next to a campsite. A 300m section of grade 2, perfect for introducing beginners to moving water at low levels. Possible to lap multiple times by walking up the river right bank. In high water the mighty Slen-bezi is unleased - surf city.
sections.directions: The turning to Slenningford Water Mill is an obvious left turn when travelling south from West Tanfield.

sections.name: Ure — Slenningford Water Mill to Ripon
sections.desc: Mostly mellow water, with a couple of shingly rapids and a playwave at the get out.
sections.directions: Put in at the Slenningford Mill site and take out on the land between the north bridge and the A61 in Ripon where the BCU has purchased some land for this purpose.

sections.name: Urr Water
sections.notes: New section Jan 2019

sections.name: Usway Burn — Davidson's Linn to Coquet Confluence
sections.desc: Exploratory paddling in the Cheviots: starts with a 10m fall followed by lots of little grade 3/4 gorges.
sections.directions: Access to the putin is via a forestry track that branches off the minor road up the Coquet at NT860114. The track passes two small farms marked as Trows and Rowhope on the OS map. Cross the ford (OK for cars at medium 0.6 gauge flows, but take care at higher levels) and follow the track up to park at the fork (NT880142). To access Davidson's Linn follow the left fork on foot, across a locked gate, and uphill through the forest for about 1.5km. After the gradient starts a slight decline take a descending path on the right for 500m to Davidson's Linn. Takeout at the confluence with the Coquet at

sections.name: Walkham — Bedford Bridge to Tavy Confluence
sections.desc: Normally combined with the Tavy, this is a fun run which starts off gently and builds up to continuous low-end grade three, with one notable slot. There's one harder grade 3 on the Tavy, just below the confluence.
sections.directions: There's a car park next to the river at Bedford Bridge. Take out at Denham Bridge on the Tavy.

sections.name: Water of Leith (Lower)
sections.notes: New calibrations April 2020, please send in more to confirm. Re-calibrated and moved to Murrayfield March 2021.

sections.name: Water of Leith (Upper)
sections.notes: New Colinton section added March 2021. Please send in calibrations to confirm.

sections.name: Water of Minnoch (Lower)
sections.notes: New lower calibrations April 2019

sections.name: Water of Minnoch (Middle)
sections.notes: New calibratons 13 April 2019

sections.name: Wear — Stanhope to Wolsingham
sections.desc: Fairly continuous grade two, with the odd bit of three, an occasional surf wave and a weir above Wolsingham.
sections.directions: Put in from the South bank of the ford at Stanhope. Get out at Hamsterly road bridge in Wolsingham, with parking at the station.

sections.name: Wear — Wearhead to Stanhope
sections.desc: Fun grade 3 run after the 6m grade 4 waterfall at the start. If running all the way to Stanhope, beware of the sticky weir above the bridge.
sections.directions: Highest put-in is at the bridge in Cowshill (technically on Killhope Burn), if you drive up from Wearhead you will see the waterfall from the road that you want to put-in above. If you don't want to run the waterfall, pr levels are low, put-in at Wearhead. Various take-outs possible, either at the bridges in Daddry Shield or Eastgate or above the ford in Stanhope.

sections.name: Wear — Wolsingham to Witton-Le-Wear
sections.desc: Small bit of grade three at the start, with a surfable wave. The gradient then eases off throughout the run.
sections.directions: Put on from the bridge at Wolsingha. Takeout river left after passing under the A68, at the minor road bridge.

sections.name: Wenning — Clapham to Hornby
sections.desc: A pleasant grade 2 touring paddle, dotted with lots of weirs and a notable playwave.
sections.directions: Putin in the centre of the village of Clapham, or 3.5km downstream at the bridge at Clapham station (a couple of beck join in between, so the the station putin may be better when low). Takeout on river left just below the bridge at Hornby.

sections.name: West Water
sections.notes: Bridge collapsed near start by Hunthill Lodge. Dangerous at low flows. See access issue link.

sections.name: West Water (new gauge)
sections.notes: New guage 2026-02 only calibrated for low and medium, needs more calibrations

sections.name: Wharfe — Barden Bridge to Bolton Bridge
sections.desc: The highlight of the run is the section preceding Bolton Abbey where the river runs through a pretty gorge which is a popular and well maintained tourist walk. This gorge contains "The Strid", which although not difficult is worth treating with care at low water due to undercuts hidden beneath the surface. Don't let this put you off though as it is easily portageable, and washes out in higher levels.
sections.directions: Put on at Barden Bridge via the public footpath. Get out on river right 100m downstream of Bolton Bridge.

sections.name: Wharfe — Bolton Bridge to Ilkley
sections.desc: Low grade bimble with a couple of weirs. The weir near Addingham may need portaging.

sections.name: Wharfe — High Bank to Hubberholme Bridge
sections.desc: Continuous spate run: the first 2km are the hardest as the river drops over a series of limestone ledges. Can be scouted from the road on the way up, so you can then blast down.
sections.directions: Takeout at Hubberholme road bridge. The road heads upstream alongside the river so you can scout on the way. When the road swings away from the river at High Bank take a small LH turn and get-on at the bridge you reach almost immediately (at the end of the road before the farm buildings).

sections.name: Wharfe — Kettlewell to Linton Falls
sections.desc: Classic Yorkshire pool-drop grade 3: a few feature drops linked by long flat sections. First drop is Conistone Falls, a 1m riverwide ledge. Next is Ghaistrills strid on a LH bend. Finally two weirs lead to Linton Falls, a grade 4 two-tier drop at the takeout.
sections.directions: Putin at Kettlewell, there is a carpark on river left just upstream of the bridge. Takeout on river right just below Linton Falls (in Linton), and scramble up the steep bank to the carpark.

sections.name: White Cart Water
sections.notes: Calibrations needed for the river (fall is calibrated separately). 0.8 should be ok to run the river below the fall.

sections.name: White Cart Water (Linn Park Fall)
sections.notes: More calibrations needed for the fall (river is calibrated separately). Dangerous when high.

sections.name: Whiteadder Water
sections.notes: Scape was 0.4 now 0.3

sections.name: Whitsundale Beck — Ravenseat to Swale Confluence
sections.desc: An interesting addition to the Upper Swale in high water. Continuous grade three with plenty of rapids hidden round blind bends.
sections.directions: Take the left turning up a small road west of Hoggarths Bridge, follow to the end and put in next to the farm yard. The beck ends at the confluence with the Upper Swale, which you'll want to paddle as well unless it's massive!

sections.name: Wye (Derbyshire) — Buxton to Litton Mill
sections.desc: Possibly the best whitewater in the Peak District? Key feature is a fun grade 3 gorge in the middle of the run.
sections.directions: Use the Car park opposite to Topley Pike quarry.

sections.name: Wyre — Abbeystead to Dolphinholme
sections.desc: From the confluence of the Tarnbrook and Marshaw Wyre's the river flows through a flat overgrown section of river into Abbeystead reservoir. The dam is yet to see a descent, for good reason, portage on the left and put back in below a small foot bridge. Two small weirs of note break up the easier water on the way down to Dolphinholme. The river continues at the same grade down at least as far as Cleveley Bridge, but this is into fishing territory, so expect hassle!

sections.name: Wyre — Tarnbrook to Abbeystead
sections.desc: Lovely small tree lined gorge until Lee Bridge, where the river passes over a small weir. Below this the river widens out and increases in volume with the addition of several small tribs. Whilst the river is best saved for in medium-high water, it becomes a terrifyingly relentless tree avoidance mission in spate.
sections.directions: From the takeout between the confluence of the two rivers at Abbeystead drive North East, taking a left turn down the hill to pass over the river at Lee Bridge where you can hop out to inspect the weir below. Turn right and drive up the river right bank. Parking is minimal, except for a large grassy area about 500m south of Tarnbrook itself. This misses out a small weir under the bridge at Ouzel Thorn, but saves hassle!

sections.name: Yarrow
sections.notes: Reported branch blocking banana slide 1 Sep 2020.

sections.name: Yealm — Mill Bridge to Mark's Bridge
sections.directions: If wanting to avoid Blachford Manor, you can miss the upper section and put in at Langham Bridge. There's not much in the way of parking spaces at either put-in or the take-out.
